By Lemma \ref{lem:simple_proj} it now follows that $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ mirrors $D$ in $P$ and that $\pmep{P}{D \mathord{\sslash} u} = \pmep{P}{D}$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Path prefix sets coincide, so mirroring and equal measures follow.

nodes.name: Emaciated projection across reductions
nodes.statement: Let $P$ be a prefix set of $s_n$ in $D$. If $s_0 = t_0 \twoheadrightarrow^\alpha t_\alpha$, then the \emph{emaciated projection} of $D$ across $t_0 \twoheadrightarrow^\alpha t_\alpha$ with respect to $P$, denoted $D \mathord{\sslash} (t_0 \twoheadrightarrow^\alpha t_\alpha)$, is defined as follows: \begin{enumerate}[(1)] \item if $\alpha = 0$, then $D \mathord{\sslash} (t_0 \twoheadrightarrow^\alpha t_\alpha) = D$, \item if $\alpha = \alpha' + 1$, then $D \mathord{\sslash} (t_0 \twoheadrightarrow^\alpha t_\alpha) = D_{\alpha'} \mathord{\sslash} (t_{\alpha'} \rightarrow t_{\alpha' + 1})$ where $D_{\alpha'} = D \mathord{\sslash} (t_0 \twoheadrightarrow^{\alpha'} t_{\alpha'})$ provided $t_{\alpha'} \rightarrow t_{\alpha' + 1}$ contracts a redex $u$ such that no redex in $u / D_{\alpha'}$ occurs at a position in $P$, \item if $\alpha$ is a limit ordinal, then $D \mathord{\sslash} (t_0 \twoheadrightarrow^\alpha t_\alpha)$ is defined as the result of applying Lemma \ref{lem:simple_proj} to $D_\beta = D \mathord{\sslash} (t_0 \twoheadrightarrow^\beta t_\beta)$, with $D \mathord{\sslash} (t_0 \twoheadrightarrow^\alpha t_\alpha)$ starting in $t_\alpha$ and with $\beta < \alpha$ such that for all $D_\gamma = D \mathord{\sslash} (t_0 \twoheadrightarrow^\gamma t_\gamma)$ with $\beta \leq \gamma < \alpha$ it holds that $\pmep{P}{D_\gamma} = \pmep{P}{D_\beta}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Emaciated projection extended transfinitely: step-wise at successors, and at limits via Lemma 4.14 once the measure stabilises.

nodes.name: Definedness of the transfinite emaciated projection
nodes.statement: Hence, the emaciated projection is only defined if the condition in the successor ordinal case is satisfied for every step along $t_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_\alpha$. The condition in the limit ordinal case can always be satisfied. This follows by Lemmas \ref{lem:essential_then_decrease} and \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal} and since $\prec$ is well-founded. In fact, by Lemma \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal} and the construction in Lemma \ref{lem:simple_proj}, it follows that choosing any $D_\beta$ satisfying the desired criteria yields the same finite sequence of complete developments for $D \mathord{\sslash} (t_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_\alpha)$.
nodes.statement_short: The limit case is always satisfiable by well-foundedness of $\prec$, and the result is independent of the chosen stage.

nodes.name: Emaciated projection example
nodes.statement: Suppose we have a fully-extended, orthogonal iCRS that has the following two rewrite rules: \begin{align*} f([x]Z(x)) & \rightarrow Z(Z(a)) \\ g(Z) & \rightarrow h(Z) \end{align*} We can now define the following finite sequence of complete developments $D$, with each development consisting of a single step: \[ g(f([x]g(g(x)))) \rightarrow g(f([x]g(h(x)))) \rightarrow g(f([x]h(h(x)))) \rightarrow g(h^4(a)) \, . \] Consider the prefix set $P = \{ \epsilon, 1 \}$ of $g(h^4(a))$, i.e.\ the set of positions of the context $g(h(\Box))$ with exception of the position of the hole. Applying the map $\varepsilon$ to $D$ with respect to $P$ yields the prefix $\{ \epsilon, 1, 10, 101 \}$, i.e.\ the set of positions of the context $g(f([x]g(\Box)))$ again with exception of the position of the hole. Hence, the $f([x]Z(x)) \rightarrow Z(Z(a))$-redex in $g(f([x]g(g(x))))$ is essential. Across that redex the emaciated projection yields the following finite sequence: \[ g^5(a) = g^5(a) \rightarrow^* g(h(g(h(g(a))))) = g(h(g(h(g(a))))) \, . \] The first complete development in the sequence becomes empty as it only contracts inessential redexes before the projection. Moreover, the last development becomes empty as the $f([x]Z(x)) \rightarrow Z(Z(a))$-redex is a residual of the contracted redex. If we next contract the redex at position $1111$ in $g^5(a)$, which is inessential with respect to the prefix set $P$ of $g(h(g(h(g(a)))))$, the emaciated projection yields the following finite sequence: \[ g^4(h(a)) = g^4(h(a)) \rightarrow g(h(g^2(h(a)))) = g(h(g^2(h(a)))) \, . \] The second complete development in the sequence no longer contracts the redex at position $111$, as that particular redex is inessential. Finally, contracting the redex at position $1$ in $g^4(h(a))$, which is essential with respect to the prefix set $P$ of $g(h(g^2(h(a))))$, the emaciated projection yields the following finite sequence: \[ g(h(g^2(h(a)))) = g(h(g^2(h(a)))) = g(h(g^2(h(a)))) = g(h(g^2(h(a)))) \, . \] The second complete development in the sequence now also becomes empty as the redex at position $1$ has already been reduced. Note that in each case the redex at the root is essential. However, the emaciated projection across contraction of this redex is undefined, as a residual of the redex occurs at a position in $P$ in the final term of each of the considered finite sequences of complete developments.
nodes.statement_short: A worked sequence of developments showing emaciated projections across essential and inessential steps, and when it is undefined.

nodes.name: Abstract projection theorem
nodes.statement: Let $O = \mathbb{N}^*$ be the set of finite tuples of natural numbers. Then there is a well-founded order $\prec$ on $O$, and a pair $(\mu, \varepsilon)$ of maps such that if $D$ is a finite sequence of complete developments and $P$ is a prefix set of the final term of $D$, then: \begin{enumerate}[$\bullet$] \item $\pmep{P}{D}$ is an element of $O$, and \item $\pmapp{P}{D}$ is a prefix set of the initial term of $D$, \end{enumerate} \noindent and if $D'$ is a sequence of complete developments strictly shorter than $D$ with $P'$ a prefix set of the final term of $D'$, then $\pmep{P'}{D'} \prec \pmep{P}{D}$. For $s \twoheadrightarrow t$, with $s$ the initial term of $D$, it further holds that: \begin{enumerate}[\em(1)] \item if $s \twoheadrightarrow t$ consists of a \emph{single} step contracting a redex $u$ at a position in $\pmapp{P}{D}$, with no residual in $u/D$ occurring at a position in $P$, then there exists a $D'$ such that $\pmep{P}{D'} \prec \pmep{P}{D}$, and \item if $s \twoheadrightarrow t$ consists of one or more steps and \emph{only} contracts redexes at positions \emph{not} in $\pmapp{P}{D}$, then there exists a $D'$ such that $\pmep{P}{D'} = \pmep{P}{D}$ and $\pmapp{P}{D'} = \pmapp{P}{D}$, \end{enumerate} where in both cases $D'$ is a finite sequence of complete developments with initial term $t$ such that the final term of $D'$ mirrors the final one of $D$ in $P$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.21
nodes.statement: \proof By Lemma \ref{compimplfinite}, $\mathcal{U}$ satisfies the finite jumps property. Hence, since $s \Rightarrow t$ and $s \Rightarrow s' \Rightarrow t$ are both complete developments of $\mathcal{U}$, we have by Theorem \ref{fjdt} that the set of descendants in $t$ of a position in $s$ is identical along both developments. By Proposition~\ref{prop:desess} it now follows for any position in $s$ with a descendant in $P$ that the position is essential irrespective of the development being either $s \Rightarrow t$ or $s \Rightarrow s' \Rightarrow t$, where the proposition is applied twice in case of the latter development. This leaves to prove that the same holds for positions in redex patterns of redexes in $\mathcal{U}$. Consider a fresh unary function symbol $f$ and replace each subterm $s'$ of $s$ with a redex from $\mathcal{U}$ occurring at the root by $f(s')$. This yields a term $s^f$. Since the unary function symbol $f$ does not occur in any of the rewrite rules of the assumed iCRS, it is easily shown for each (not necessarily complete) development starting in $s$ that there exists a corresponding development starting in $s^f$, where the set of redexes is adapted appropriately and such that the removal of all function symbols $f$ yields the original development. Hence, the completeness of a development starting in $s$ implies the completeness of the corresponding development starting in $s^f$. Suppose that $s^f \Rightarrow t^f$ is the complete development that corresponds to $s \Rightarrow t$. Define the prefix set $P^f$ of $t^f$ in such a way that the removal of the function symbols $f$ from $t^f$ and the corresponding elements from the positions in $P^f$ yields $P$ and such that for any position $p \in P^f$ that is not the prefix of any another position in $P^f$ it holds that $\rs{t^f|_p} \not = f$. By definition of $P^f$ and the definition of essentiality, a redex in $\mathcal{U}$ is essential if and only if the function symbol $f$ directly preceding it in $s^f$ is. Hence, by looking at the function symbols $f$ occurring in $s^f$, the result now follows for the positions in the redex patterns of the redexes in $\mathcal{U}$ in similar fashion as for all other positions. \qed
nodes.statement_short: Descendants agree by the Finite Jumps Developments Theorem, handling ordinary positions; redex-pattern positions are handled by marking redexes with a fresh unary symbol $f$.

$s \rightarrow t$ contracts a redex $u$ such that no redex in either $u / D$ or $u / E$ occurs at a position in $P$
conclusions: $E \mathord{\sslash} u$ mirrors $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ in $P$
nodes.label: lem:nf_mirror

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.25
nodes.statement: \proof Suppose $s \rightarrow t$ contracts a redex $u$ such that no redex in either $u / D$ or $u / E$ occurs at a position in $P$. Let $D'$ and $E'$ be the result of applying Lemma \ref{lem:simple_proj} to $D$ and $E$, respectively, with $D'$ and $E'$ both starting in $s$. By construction and since $E$ mirrors $D$ in $P$, it follows that $D'$ and $E'$ are identical. Hence, $D' / u$ and $E' / u$ are identical and, by the definition of the emaciated projection, $E \mathord{\sslash} u$ mirrors $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ in $P$. \qed
nodes.statement_short: The cut-downs of $D$ and $E$ by Lemma 4.14 coincide, hence so do their projections.

nodes.name: Cut down both sequences
nodes.statement: Suppose $s \rightarrow t$ contracts a redex $u$ such that no redex in either $u / D$ or $u / E$ occurs at a position in $P$. Let $D'$ and $E'$ be the result of applying Lemma \ref{lem:simple_proj} to $D$ and $E$, respectively, with $D'$ and $E'$ both starting in $s$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 4.14 to $D$ and $E$.

nodes.name: Cut-downs coincide
nodes.statement: By construction and since $E$ mirrors $D$ in $P$, it follows that $D'$ and $E'$ are identical.
nodes.statement_short: Mirroring makes the cut-downs identical.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence, $D' / u$ and $E' / u$ are identical and, by the definition of the emaciated projection, $E \mathord{\sslash} u$ mirrors $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ in $P$.
nodes.statement_short: Identical projections give mirroring of the emaciated projections.

nodes.name: Sub-mirroring
nodes.statement: Let $P$ and $Q$ with $Q \subseteq P$ be prefix sets of, respectively, $s_n$ in $D$ and $t_n$ in $E$. The finite sequence $E$ \emph{sub-mirrors} $D$ in $Q \subseteq P$ if for all $0 \leq i \leq n$ it holds that $Q_i \subseteq P_i$, $t_i$ mirrors $s_i$ in $Q_i$, and the path prefix set of $Q_i$ with respect to $\mathcal{V}_i$ is a subset of the path prefix set of $P_i$ with respect to $\mathcal{U}_i$.

nodes.name: Emaciated projections w.r.t. smaller prefix sets sub-mirror
nodes.statement: Let $D$ be a finite sequence of complete developments starting in a term $s$. Moreover, let $P$ and $P'$ be prefix sets of the final term of $D$ such that $P' \subseteq P$. If $s \rightarrow t$ contracts a redex $u$ such that no redex in $u / D$ occurs at a position in $P$, then $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ with respect to $P'$ sub-mirrors $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ with respect to $P$.
assumptions: $D$ be a finite sequence of complete developments starting in a term $s$
$P$ and $P'$ be prefix sets of the final term of $D$ such that $P' \subseteq P$
$s \rightarrow t$ contracts a redex $u$ such that no redex in $u / D$ occurs at a position in $P$
conclusions: $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ with respect to $P'$ sub-mirrors $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ with respect to $P$
nodes.label: lem:nf_submirror

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.27
nodes.statement: \proof Suppose $s \rightarrow t$ contracts a redex $u$ such that no redex in $u / D$ occurs at a position in $P$. Hence, since $P' \subseteq P$, no redex in $u / D$ occurs at a position in $P'$ either. Let $E$ and $E'$ be the result of applying Lemma \ref{lem:simple_proj} to $D$ with respect to $P$ and $P'$, respectively, such that $E$ and $E'$ start in $s$. By construction, $E'$ sub-mirrors $E$ in $P' \subseteq P$. Moreover, no redex in $u /E$, respectively $u / E'$, occurs at a position in $P$, respectively in $P'$. Let $s_0 = s'_0 = s$ and $t_0 = t'_0 = t$ and write $E : \fscd{s}{U}{n}$ and $E' : \fscdp{s}{U}{n}$. Consider the following two diagrams, which are the result of iteratively applying Proposition \ref{prop:finite_over_normal} to $E$ and $E'$, respectively. \[ \xymatrix@=0.78cm{ s_0 \ar@{=>}[r] \ar[d]^{u} & s_1 \ar@{=>}[r] \ar@{=>}[d] & \cdot \ar@{.}[r] \ar@{=>}[d] & \cdot \ar@{=>}[r] & s_n \ar@{=>}[d]^{u / E} & s'_0 \ar@{=>}[r] \ar[d]^{u} & s'_1 \ar@{=>}[r] \ar@{=>}[d] & \cdot \ar@{.}[r] \ar@{=>}[d] & \cdot \ar@{=>}[r] & s'_n \ar@{=>}[d]^{u / E'} \\ t_0 \ar@{=>}[r] & t_1 \ar@{=>}[r] & \cdot \ar@{.}[r] & \cdot \ar@{=>}[r] & t_n & t'_0 \ar@{=>}[r] & t'_1 \ar@{=>}[r] & \cdot \ar@{.}[r] & \cdot \ar@{=>}[r] & t'_n } \] Let $P_i$, respectively $P'_i$, be the set of positions essential for $P$ in $s_i$, respectively for $P'$ in $s'_i$. Since $E'$ sub-mirrors $E$ in $P' \subseteq P$, it follows for all $0 \leq i \leq n$ that $P'_i \subseteq P_i$. Moreover, for each redex in $u / (s'_0 \Rightarrow^* s'_i)$ that occurs at a position in $P'_i$ it follows that there exists a redex in $u / (s_0 \Rightarrow^* s_i)$ that occurs at the same position. In addition, it holds for each such redex that all positions in its redex pattern occur in $P'_i$, otherwise a redex in $u / E'$ occurs at a position in $P'$. By induction, employing the definition of descendants and the above facts, it follows that $t'_i$ mirrors $t_i$ in $P'_i / (s'_i \Rightarrow t'_i) \subseteq P_i / (s_i \Rightarrow t_i)$. Moreover, by fully-extendedness and orthogonality we have for each redex in $\mathcal{U}'_i / (s'_i \Rightarrow t'_i)$ that there exists a redex in $t_i$ at the same position and employing the same rewrite rule. And, since $E'$ sub-mirrors $E$ in $P' \subseteq P$, it also follows for each redex in $\mathcal{U}_i / (s_i \Rightarrow t_i)$ that if all positions in its redex pattern occur in $P_i / (s_i \Rightarrow t_i)$ but some do not occur in $P'_i / (s'_i \Rightarrow t'_i)$, then in fact no position of the redex pattern occurs in $P'_i / (s'_i \Rightarrow t'_i)$. Since $t_n$ mirrors $s_n$ in $P$, respectively $t'_n$ mirrors $s'_n$ in $P'$, it follows by induction, applying Proposition \ref{prop:desess}, that $P_i / (s_i \Rightarrow t_i)$, respectively $P'_i / (s'_i \Rightarrow t'_i)$, is in fact the set of position essential for $P$ in $t_i$, respectively the set of position essential for $P'$ in $t'_i$. Hence, $E' / u$ sub-mirrors $E / u$ in $P' \subseteq P$. That $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ with respect to $P'$ sub-mirrors $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ with respect to $P$ now follows by definition of the emaciated projection. \qed
nodes.statement_short: Cut down $D$ w.r.t. $P$ and $P'$, project both over $u$ by Proposition 2.27, and show by induction that sub-mirroring is preserved tile by tile.

nodes.name: Cut down w.r.t. both prefix sets
nodes.statement: Suppose $s \rightarrow t$ contracts a redex $u$ such that no redex in $u / D$ occurs at a position in $P$. Hence, since $P' \subseteq P$, no redex in $u / D$ occurs at a position in $P'$ either. Let $E$ and $E'$ be the result of applying Lemma \ref{lem:simple_proj} to $D$ with respect to $P$ and $P'$, respectively, such that $E$ and $E'$ start in $s$. By construction, $E'$ sub-mirrors $E$ in $P' \subseteq P$. Moreover, no redex in $u /E$, respectively $u / E'$, occurs at a position in $P$, respectively in $P'$.
nodes.statement_short: Cut down $D$ w.r.t. $P$ and $P'$; the cut-downs sub-mirror.

nodes.name: Projection diagrams
nodes.statement: Let $s_0 = s'_0 = s$ and $t_0 = t'_0 = t$ and write $E : \fscd{s}{U}{n}$ and $E' : \fscdp{s}{U}{n}$. Consider the following two diagrams, which are the result of iteratively applying Proposition \ref{prop:finite_over_normal} to $E$ and $E'$, respectively. \[ \xymatrix@=0.78cm{ s_0 \ar@{=>}[r] \ar[d]^{u} & s_1 \ar@{=>}[r] \ar@{=>}[d] & \cdot \ar@{.}[r] \ar@{=>}[d] & \cdot \ar@{=>}[r] & s_n \ar@{=>}[d]^{u / E} & s'_0 \ar@{=>}[r] \ar[d]^{u} & s'_1 \ar@{=>}[r] \ar@{=>}[d] & \cdot \ar@{.}[r] \ar@{=>}[d] & \cdot \ar@{=>}[r] & s'_n \ar@{=>}[d]^{u / E'} \\ t_0 \ar@{=>}[r] & t_1 \ar@{=>}[r] & \cdot \ar@{.}[r] & \cdot \ar@{=>}[r] & t_n & t'_0 \ar@{=>}[r] & t'_1 \ar@{=>}[r] & \cdot \ar@{.}[r] & \cdot \ar@{=>}[r] & t'_n } \]
nodes.statement_short: Project both cut-downs over $u$ via Proposition 2.27.

nodes.name: Residuals in essential sets
nodes.statement: Let $P_i$, respectively $P'_i$, be the set of positions essential for $P$ in $s_i$, respectively for $P'$ in $s'_i$. Since $E'$ sub-mirrors $E$ in $P' \subseteq P$, it follows for all $0 \leq i \leq n$ that $P'_i \subseteq P_i$. Moreover, for each redex in $u / (s'_0 \Rightarrow^* s'_i)$ that occurs at a position in $P'_i$ it follows that there exists a redex in $u / (s_0 \Rightarrow^* s_i)$ that occurs at the same position. In addition, it holds for each such redex that all positions in its redex pattern occur in $P'_i$, otherwise a redex in $u / E'$ occurs at a position in $P'$.
nodes.statement_short: Essential sets are nested and residuals of $u$ in $P'_i$ correspond.

nodes.name: Mirroring of projected terms
nodes.statement: By induction, employing the definition of descendants and the above facts, it follows that $t'_i$ mirrors $t_i$ in $P'_i / (s'_i \Rightarrow t'_i) \subseteq P_i / (s_i \Rightarrow t_i)$. Moreover, by fully-extendedness and orthogonality we have for each redex in $\mathcal{U}'_i / (s'_i \Rightarrow t'_i)$ that there exists a redex in $t_i$ at the same position and employing the same rewrite rule. And, since $E'$ sub-mirrors $E$ in $P' \subseteq P$, it also follows for each redex in $\mathcal{U}_i / (s_i \Rightarrow t_i)$ that if all positions in its redex pattern occur in $P_i / (s_i \Rightarrow t_i)$ but some do not occur in $P'_i / (s'_i \Rightarrow t'_i)$, then in fact no position of the redex pattern occurs in $P'_i / (s'_i \Rightarrow t'_i)$.
nodes.statement_short: By induction the projected terms mirror on descendant sets.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Since $t_n$ mirrors $s_n$ in $P$, respectively $t'_n$ mirrors $s'_n$ in $P'$, it follows by induction, applying Proposition \ref{prop:desess}, that $P_i / (s_i \Rightarrow t_i)$, respectively $P'_i / (s'_i \Rightarrow t'_i)$, is in fact the set of position essential for $P$ in $t_i$, respectively the set of position essential for $P'$ in $t'_i$. Hence, $E' / u$ sub-mirrors $E / u$ in $P' \subseteq P$. That $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ with respect to $P'$ sub-mirrors $D \mathord{\sslash} u$ with respect to $P$ now follows by definition of the emaciated projection.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 4.10 identifies the essential sets; sub-mirroring follows.

nodes.name: Emaciated projections of reductions to normal form are defined
nodes.statement: Let $s_0 \rightarrow^* s_1 \rightarrow^* \cdots \rightarrow^* s_d \rightarrow^* \cdots \, s_\omega$ be a reduction to normal form of length at most $\omega$ such that, for all $d \in \mathbb{N}$, the steps in $s_d \twoheadrightarrow s_\omega$ occur below depth $d$ and $P_d$ is the set of positions in $s_d$ above depth $d$. For every $s_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_0$, redex $u$ in $t_0$, and $d \in \mathbb{N}$ no redex in $u / D_d$ occurs at a position in $P_d$, with $D_d = (s_0 \rightarrow^* s_d) \mathord{\sslash} (s_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_0)$ with respect to~$P_d$.
assumptions: $s_0 \rightarrow^* s_1 \rightarrow^* \cdots \rightarrow^* s_d \rightarrow^* \cdots \, s_\omega$ be a reduction to normal form of length at most $\omega$ such that, for all $d \in \mathbb{N}$, the steps in $s_d \twoheadrightarrow s_\omega$ occur below depth $d$ and $P_d$ is the set of positions in $s_d$ above depth $d$
conclusions: For every $s_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_0$, redex $u$ in $t_0$, and $d \in \mathbb{N}$ no redex in $u / D_d$ occurs at a position in $P_d$
nodes.statement_short: Along a reduction to normal form, the emaciated projection of each finite prefix over any reduction is always defined.
nodes.label: lem:nf_ok

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.28
nodes.statement: \proof We reason by contradiction. Thus, suppose a reduction $s_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_0$, redex $u$ in $t_0$, and $d \in \mathbb{N}$ exist such that a redex in $u / D_d$ occurs at a position in $P_d$, with $D_d = (s \rightarrow^* s_d) \mathord{\sslash} (s_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_0)$. Note that $D_d$ is defined, otherwise there is a reduction shorter than $s_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_0$ satisfying the required conditions. Assume $s \rightarrow^* s_d$ has length $n$. Moreover, let $k$ be the maximum value $|p|$ with $p$ a position in the redex pattern of the rule employed in $u$ and assume $s \rightarrow^* s_{d + k}$ has length~$m$. Write $E_d$, respectively $E_{d + k}$, for $(s_0 \rightarrow^* s_{d + k}) \mathord{\sslash} (s_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_0)$ with respect to $P_d$, respectively $P_{d + k}$. By ordinal induction on the length of $s \twoheadrightarrow t$, applying Lemma \ref{lem:nf_mirror} with respect to $P_d$ and Lemma \ref{lem:nf_submirror} with respect to $P_d \subseteq P_{d + k}$, it follows that $E_d$ sub-mirrors $E_{d + k}$ in $P_d \subseteq P_{d + k}$. Moreover, by definition of emaciated projections and since all steps in $s_d \rightarrow^* s_{d + k}$ occur below depth $d$, we have that $D_d$ mirrors the sequence of the first $n$ developments of $E_d$ in $P_d$ and that all steps in the last $m - n$ developments of $E_d$ and $E_{d + k}$ occur below depth $d$. By orthogonality and fully-extendedness, it follows for the redex in $u / D_d$, which occurs at a position $p \in P_d$ in the final term of $D_d$, that a redex in $u / E_d$ occurs at $p$ in the final term of $E_d$. Moreover, since $E_d$ sub-mirrors $E_{d + k}$, this implies that a redex in $u / E_{d + k}$ occurs at $p$ in the final term of $E_{d + k}$. But then, since the final term of $E_{d + k}$ mirrors $s_{d + k}$ in $P_{d + k}$, it holds for $s_{d + k}$ that a redex and all the positions in its redex pattern occur in $P_{d + k}$, which is impossible by definition of $s_{d + k}$, contradiction. \qed
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction with a minimal counterexample. Going $k$ levels deeper with Lemmas 4.25 and 4.27 transports the offending redex into $s_{d+k}$, impossible above depth $d+k$.

nodes.name: Assume a counterexample
nodes.statement: We reason by contradiction. Thus, suppose a reduction $s_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_0$, redex $u$ in $t_0$, and $d \in \mathbb{N}$ exist such that a redex in $u / D_d$ occurs at a position in $P_d$, with $D_d = (s \rightarrow^* s_d) \mathord{\sslash} (s_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_0)$. Note that $D_d$ is defined, otherwise there is a reduction shorter than $s_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_0$ satisfying the required conditions.
nodes.statement_short: Assume a shortest reduction with a residual of $u$ in $P_d$.

nodes.name: Lengths and pattern depth
nodes.statement: Assume $s \rightarrow^* s_d$ has length $n$. Moreover, let $k$ be the maximum value $|p|$ with $p$ a position in the redex pattern of the rule employed in $u$ and assume $s \rightarrow^* s_{d + k}$ has length~$m$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix lengths $n,m$ and the redex-pattern depth $k$.

nodes.name: Derive contradiction
nodes.statement: Write $E_d$, respectively $E_{d + k}$, for $(s_0 \rightarrow^* s_{d + k}) \mathord{\sslash} (s_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_0)$ with respect to $P_d$, respectively $P_{d + k}$. By ordinal induction on the length of $s \twoheadrightarrow t$, applying Lemma \ref{lem:nf_mirror} with respect to $P_d$ and Lemma \ref{lem:nf_submirror} with respect to $P_d \subseteq P_{d + k}$, it follows that $E_d$ sub-mirrors $E_{d + k}$ in $P_d \subseteq P_{d + k}$. Moreover, by definition of emaciated projections and since all steps in $s_d \rightarrow^* s_{d + k}$ occur below depth $d$, we have that $D_d$ mirrors the sequence of the first $n$ developments of $E_d$ in $P_d$ and that all steps in the last $m - n$ developments of $E_d$ and $E_{d + k}$ occur below depth $d$. By orthogonality and fully-extendedness, it follows for the redex in $u / D_d$, which occurs at a position $p \in P_d$ in the final term of $D_d$, that a redex in $u / E_d$ occurs at $p$ in the final term of $E_d$. Moreover, since $E_d$ sub-mirrors $E_{d + k}$, this implies that a redex in $u / E_{d + k}$ occurs at $p$ in the final term of $E_{d + k}$. But then, since the final term of $E_{d + k}$ mirrors $s_{d + k}$ in $P_{d + k}$, it holds for $s_{d + k}$ that a redex and all the positions in its redex pattern occur in $P_{d + k}$, which is impossible by definition of $s_{d + k}$, contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Sub-mirroring transports the redex to $s_{d+k}$ within $P_{d+k}$, a contradiction.

nodes.name: Sub-mirroring by ordinal induction
nodes.statement: Write $E_d$, respectively $E_{d + k}$, for $(s_0 \rightarrow^* s_{d + k}) \mathord{\sslash} (s_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_0)$ with respect to $P_d$, respectively $P_{d + k}$. By ordinal induction on the length of $s \twoheadrightarrow t$, applying Lemma \ref{lem:nf_mirror} with respect to $P_d$ and Lemma \ref{lem:nf_submirror} with respect to $P_d \subseteq P_{d + k}$, it follows that $E_d$ sub-mirrors $E_{d + k}$ in $P_d \subseteq P_{d + k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemmas 4.25 and 4.27 by ordinal induction give sub-mirroring.

nodes.name: Deep steps
nodes.statement: Moreover, by definition of emaciated projections and since all steps in $s_d \rightarrow^* s_{d + k}$ occur below depth $d$, we have that $D_d$ mirrors the sequence of the first $n$ developments of $E_d$ in $P_d$ and that all steps in the last $m - n$ developments of $E_d$ and $E_{d + k}$ occur below depth $d$.
nodes.statement_short: $D_d$ mirrors the start of $E_d$; extra developments lie below depth $d$.

nodes.name: Transport the redex
nodes.statement: By orthogonality and fully-extendedness, it follows for the redex in $u / D_d$, which occurs at a position $p \in P_d$ in the final term of $D_d$, that a redex in $u / E_d$ occurs at $p$ in the final term of $E_d$. Moreover, since $E_d$ sub-mirrors $E_{d + k}$, this implies that a redex in $u / E_{d + k}$ occurs at $p$ in the final term of $E_{d + k}$.
nodes.statement_short: The residual of $u$ appears at $p$ in $E_d$ and $E_{d+k}$.

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement: But then, since the final term of $E_{d + k}$ mirrors $s_{d + k}$ in $P_{d + k}$, it holds for $s_{d + k}$ that a redex and all the positions in its redex pattern occur in $P_{d + k}$, which is impossible by definition of $s_{d + k}$, contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Then $s_{d+k}$ has a redex inside $P_{d+k}$, impossible.

nodes.name: Normal form
nodes.statement: A term in an iCRS is a \emph{normal form} if no redexes occur in the term.
differentia: no redexes occur in the term

nodes.name: P-fair reduction
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a predicate. A \emph{$\mathcal{P}$-fair reduction} is a weakly continuous reduction $(s_\beta)_{\beta < \alpha}$ where for every $\beta < \alpha$ and redex $u$ in $s_\beta$ satisfying $\mathcal{P}$ there exists a $\beta \leq \gamma < \min ( \alpha, \beta + \omega )$ such that either \begin{enumerate}[(1)] \item $s_\gamma \rightarrow s_{\gamma + 1}$ contracts a residual of $u$ satisfying $\mathcal{P}$, or \item no residual of $u$ in $s_\gamma$ satisfies $\mathcal{P}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: A weakly continuous reduction in which every redex satisfying $\mathcal{P}$ is, within finitely many steps, contracted or stops satisfying $\mathcal{P}$.
nodes.label: def:pfair

nodes.name: Weak continuity prevents cheating
nodes.statement: The condition that a fair reduction should be weakly continuous is simply a safeguard against reduction strategies that are normalising only by cheating. For example, in the iCRS which has the rules $a \rightarrow a$ and $b \rightarrow f(b)$, the reduction \[ a \rightarrow a \rightarrow \cdots \, b \rightarrow f(b) \rightarrow \cdots \, f^\omega \] is normalising, but none of the terms in the first $\omega$ steps bear any relationship to the final term as the reduction is not weakly continuous, let alone convergent.

nodes.name: Outermost-fair and non-outermost-fair reductions
nodes.statement: Given that a redex at a position $p$ is called outermost if no redex occurs at a strict prefix position of $p$, we can define \emph{outermost-fair} reductions by defining a predicate on redexes that is true in case the redex is outermost and false otherwise. Consider the following two rewrite rules: \begin{align*} f(Z) & \rightarrow g(Z) \\ a & \rightarrow g(a) \end{align*} Next, consider the reductions \[ f(a) \rightarrow f(g(a)) \rightarrow \cdots \rightarrow f(g^n(a)) \rightarrow g^{n + 1}(a) \rightarrow \cdots \, g^\omega \] and \[ f(a) \rightarrow f(g(a)) \rightarrow \cdots \rightarrow f(g^n(a)) \rightarrow \cdots \, f(g^\omega) \rightarrow g^\omega \, . \] The first of these reductions is outermost-fair, as a residual of each redex present in each term is reduced after a finite number of steps. The second reduction is \emph{not} outermost-fair, as a residual of a redex that occurs at the root of $f(a)$ is only contracted after $\omega$ steps and as a redex occurring at the root of a term is always outermost.
nodes.label: ex:outfair

nodes.name: Outermost redex and outermost-fair reduction
nodes.statement: Let $s$ be a term. A redex at a position $p$ in $s$ is \emph{outermost} if no redex in $s$ occurs at a strict prefix position of $p$. The predicate $\Parg{outermost}$ is satisfied by a redex if{f} that redex is outermost. An \emph{outermost-fair reduction} is a $\Parg{outermost}$-fair reduction.

nodes.name: Outermost-fair reductions converge to the normal form
nodes.statement: Let $s$ be a term and $T$ an outermost-fair reduction of length at least $\omega$ starting in $s$. If there is a reduction $s \twoheadrightarrow t$ to normal form, then $T$ is strongly convergent of length $\omega$ with $t$ as its final term.
assumptions: $s$ be a term and $T$ an outermost-fair reduction of length at least $\omega$ starting in $s$
there is a reduction $s \twoheadrightarrow t$ to normal form
conclusions: $T$ is strongly convergent of length $\omega$ with $t$ as its final term
nodes.label: lem:outermost_help

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.6
nodes.statement: \proof By compression, we may assume that $s \twoheadrightarrow t$ has length at most $\omega$. Moreover, by strong convergence we may write $s \twoheadrightarrow t$ as: \[ s \rightarrow^* s_1 \rightarrow^* \cdots \rightarrow^* s_d \rightarrow^* \cdots \, t \, , \] where all steps in $s_d \twoheadrightarrow t$ occur below depth $d$. For each depth $d > 0$ and $D_d : s \rightarrow^* s_d$, we have by definition that $s_d$ mirrors $t$ in $P_d$, where $P_d$ is the set of positions in $t$ above depth $d$. Moreover, no redexes occur in $s_d$ at positions in $P_d$ and, as $s \rightarrow^* s_d$ is finite, we can view $D_d$ to be a finite sequence of complete developments, where each development consists of a single step. Let the depth $d > 0$ be arbitrary and denote the first $\omega$ steps of $T$ by $T_\omega$. Consider $D_d \mathord{\sslash} T_\omega$, which exists by Lemma \ref{lem:nf_ok}. By Lemmas~\ref{lem:essential_then_decrease} and \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal} and well-foundedness of $\prec$, only a finite number of steps of $T_\omega$ is essential for $P_d$. Following the finite number of essential steps, there are two possibilities for the emaciated projection of $D_d$ by the construction in Lemma \ref{lem:simple_proj}: Either all developments in the projection are empty, or not. \begin{enumerate}[$\bullet$] \item In case all developments are empty it follows by Lemma \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal} that all remaining terms along $T_\omega$ mirror $s_d$ and $t$ in $P_d$ and that no redexes are contracted above depth $d$. \item In case not all developments are empty, it follows by Lemma \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal} that there exists a fixed set of essential positions $P$ such that all the remaining terms along $T_\omega$ mirror each other in $P$. Moreover, the lemma together with non-emptiness implies that a redex $u$ occurs at a fixed position in $P$. Since the depth of $u$ is finite, only a finite number of redexes can be created above $u$ in the remaining part of $T_\omega$. These redexes cannot be contracted or cease to exist by orthogonality and since all further contracted redexes occur at positions not in $P$, again by Lemma \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal}. Hence, after a finite number of further steps a redex must be created that is outermost for the remainder of $T_\omega$, contradicting outermost-fairness. Thus, the emaciated projection of $D_d$ must become empty after a finite number of steps. \end{enumerate} As the previous holds for all depths $d > 0$, we have that $T_\omega$ is strongly convergent with limit $t$. Hence, $T = T_\omega$ and the result follows. \qed
nodes.statement_short: For each depth $d$, project the prefix $D_d$ of the normalising reduction along $T$; only finitely many steps are essential, and a non-empty projection would leave an outermost redex uncontracted, contradicting fairness.

nodes.name: Compress and stratify
nodes.statement: By compression, we may assume that $s \twoheadrightarrow t$ has length at most $\omega$. Moreover, by strong convergence we may write $s \twoheadrightarrow t$ as: \[ s \rightarrow^* s_1 \rightarrow^* \cdots \rightarrow^* s_d \rightarrow^* \cdots \, t \, , \] where all steps in $s_d \twoheadrightarrow t$ occur below depth $d$.
nodes.statement_short: By compression the normalising reduction has length at most $\omega$, stratified by depth.

nodes.name: Prefix reductions
nodes.statement: For each depth $d > 0$ and $D_d : s \rightarrow^* s_d$, we have by definition that $s_d$ mirrors $t$ in $P_d$, where $P_d$ is the set of positions in $t$ above depth $d$. Moreover, no redexes occur in $s_d$ at positions in $P_d$ and, as $s \rightarrow^* s_d$ is finite, we can view $D_d$ to be a finite sequence of complete developments, where each development consists of a single step.
nodes.statement_short: $s_d$ mirrors $t$ above depth $d$ and $D_d$ is a finite sequence of developments.

nodes.name: Projection along T becomes empty
nodes.statement: Let the depth $d > 0$ be arbitrary and denote the first $\omega$ steps of $T$ by $T_\omega$. Consider $D_d \mathord{\sslash} T_\omega$, which exists by Lemma \ref{lem:nf_ok}. By Lemmas~\ref{lem:essential_then_decrease} and \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal} and well-foundedness of $\prec$, only a finite number of steps of $T_\omega$ is essential for $P_d$. Following the finite number of essential steps, there are two possibilities for the emaciated projection of $D_d$ by the construction in Lemma \ref{lem:simple_proj}: Either all developments in the projection are empty, or not. \begin{enumerate}[$\bullet$] \item In case all developments are empty it follows by Lemma \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal} that all remaining terms along $T_\omega$ mirror $s_d$ and $t$ in $P_d$ and that no redexes are contracted above depth $d$. \item In case not all developments are empty, it follows by Lemma \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal} that there exists a fixed set of essential positions $P$ such that all the remaining terms along $T_\omega$ mirror each other in $P$. Moreover, the lemma together with non-emptiness implies that a redex $u$ occurs at a fixed position in $P$. Since the depth of $u$ is finite, only a finite number of redexes can be created above $u$ in the remaining part of $T_\omega$. These redexes cannot be contracted or cease to exist by orthogonality and since all further contracted redexes occur at positions not in $P$, again by Lemma \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal}. Hence, after a finite number of further steps a redex must be created that is outermost for the remainder of $T_\omega$, contradicting outermost-fairness. Thus, the emaciated projection of $D_d$ must become empty after a finite number of steps.
nodes.statement_short: Project $D_d$ along $T_\omega$; in both cases the projection becomes empty.

nodes.name: Project D_d
nodes.statement: Let the depth $d > 0$ be arbitrary and denote the first $\omega$ steps of $T$ by $T_\omega$. Consider $D_d \mathord{\sslash} T_\omega$, which exists by Lemma \ref{lem:nf_ok}.
nodes.statement_short: Consider $D_d \sslash T_\omega$, defined by Lemma 4.28.

nodes.name: Finitely many essential steps
nodes.statement: By Lemmas~\ref{lem:essential_then_decrease} and \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal} and well-foundedness of $\prec$, only a finite number of steps of $T_\omega$ is essential for $P_d$.
nodes.statement_short: Measure decrease and well-foundedness bound the essential steps.

nodes.name: Two possibilities
nodes.statement: Following the finite number of essential steps, there are two possibilities for the emaciated projection of $D_d$ by the construction in Lemma \ref{lem:simple_proj}: Either all developments in the projection are empty, or not.
nodes.statement_short: Either all developments in the projection are empty or not.

nodes.name: All empty
nodes.statement: In case all developments are empty it follows by Lemma \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal} that all remaining terms along $T_\omega$ mirror $s_d$ and $t$ in $P_d$ and that no redexes are contracted above depth $d$.
nodes.statement_short: Then the remaining terms mirror $t$ above depth $d$.

nodes.name: Not all empty
nodes.statement: In case not all developments are empty, it follows by Lemma \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal} that there exists a fixed set of essential positions $P$ such that all the remaining terms along $T_\omega$ mirror each other in $P$. Moreover, the lemma together with non-emptiness implies that a redex $u$ occurs at a fixed position in $P$. Since the depth of $u$ is finite, only a finite number of redexes can be created above $u$ in the remaining part of $T_\omega$. These redexes cannot be contracted or cease to exist by orthogonality and since all further contracted redexes occur at positions not in $P$, again by Lemma \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal}. Hence, after a finite number of further steps a redex must be created that is outermost for the remainder of $T_\omega$, contradicting outermost-fairness. Thus, the emaciated projection of $D_d$ must become empty after a finite number of steps.
nodes.statement_short: A persistent redex forces an eventually outermost redex never contracted, contradicting fairness.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: As the previous holds for all depths $d > 0$, we have that $T_\omega$ is strongly convergent with limit $t$. Hence, $T = T_\omega$ and the result follows.
nodes.statement_short: For all depths, $T_\omega$ converges strongly to $t$.

nodes.name: Outermost-fair strategies are normalising
nodes.statement: If $s$ can be reduced to normal form by a strongly convergent reduction, then it also reduces to a normal form by any outermost-fair reduction. Any such reduction is strongly convergent and of length at most $\omega$.
assumptions: $s$ can be reduced to normal form by a strongly convergent reduction
conclusions: it also reduces to a normal form by any outermost-fair reduction
Any such reduction is strongly convergent and of length at most $\omega$.
nodes.label: thm:outermostfair

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.7
nodes.statement: \proof If $T$ is a finite outermost-fair reduction starting in $s$ and $T$ reaches a normal form, then we are done. If $T$ is finite but has not reached a normal form, then there is at least one outermost redex in the final term of $T$, and we may thus extend it. Hence, we only need to prove that if $T$ is infinite, then $T$ is strongly convergent of length $\omega$ and reaches a normal form. This is the content of Lemma \ref{lem:outermost_help}. \qed
nodes.statement_short: Finite outermost-fair reductions can be extended until a normal form; the infinite case is Lemma 5.6.

nodes.name: Finite and normal
nodes.statement: If $T$ is a finite outermost-fair reduction starting in $s$ and $T$ reaches a normal form, then we are done.
nodes.statement_short: A finite reduction reaching a normal form is done.

nodes.name: Finite, not normal
nodes.statement: If $T$ is finite but has not reached a normal form, then there is at least one outermost redex in the final term of $T$, and we may thus extend it.
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise an outermost redex remains and $T$ extends.

nodes.name: Infinite case
nodes.statement: Hence, we only need to prove that if $T$ is infinite, then $T$ is strongly convergent of length $\omega$ and reaches a normal form. This is the content of Lemma \ref{lem:outermost_help}.
nodes.statement_short: The infinite case is Lemma 5.6.

nodes.name: Fair reduction
nodes.statement: Let $\Parg{true}$ be the predicate that is true on all redexes in all terms. A \emph{fair reduction} is a $\Parg{true}$-fair reduction.

nodes.name: Second fairness clause vacuous for fair reductions
nodes.statement: As the predicate is always true, the second clause of Definition \ref{def:pfair} cannot occur in a fair reduction unless the first clause applies earlier in the considered reduction.

nodes.name: Fair strategies are normalising
nodes.statement: If $s$ can be reduced to a normal form by a strongly convergent reduction, then it also reduces to a normal form by any fair reduction. Any such reduction is strongly convergent and of length at most $\omega$.
assumptions: $s$ can be reduced to a normal form by a strongly convergent reduction
conclusions: it also reduces to a normal form by any fair reduction
Any such reduction is strongly convergent and of length at most $\omega$.
nodes.label: thm:fair

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.9
nodes.statement: \proof Since a fair reduction is in particular fair with respect to outermost redexes, the result follows by Theorem \ref{thm:outermostfair}. \qed
nodes.statement_short: A fair reduction is outermost-fair, so Theorem 5.7 applies.

nodes.name: Fairness result is weaker
nodes.statement: As each fair reduction is an outermost-fair reduction, it follows that the predicate that is true on all redexes in all terms strengthens the predicate used for outermost-fair reductions. Hence, we obtained a weaker result than in the previous section.

nodes.name: Needed redex and needed-fair reduction
nodes.statement: Let $s$ be a term. A redex $u$ in $s$ is \emph{needed} if, along every strongly convergent reduction from $s$ to a normal form, some residual of $u$ is contracted. The predicate $\Parg{needed}$ is satisfied by a redex if{f} that redex is needed. A \emph{needed-fair reduction} is a $\Parg{needed}$-fair reduction.
nodes.statement_short: A redex is needed if every strongly convergent reduction to normal form contracts a residual of it; needed-fair is $\Parg{needed}$-fair.

nodes.name: Second fairness clause vacuous for needed-fair reductions
nodes.statement: By definition of neededness, the second clause of Definition \ref{def:pfair} cannot occur in a needed-fair reduction unless the first clause applies earlier on in the considered reduction, otherwise the considered redex is not needed.

nodes.name: Needed-fair and non-needed-fair reductions
nodes.statement: Consider the rewrite rules and reductions from Example \ref{ex:outfair}. The first reduction is needed-fair, as each redex along the reduction is reduced after a finite number of steps. The second reduction is not needed-fair, as the redex at the root of $f(a)$ is only reduced after $\omega$ steps and as the redex at the root of a term is by definition needed.

nodes.name: Essential redexes are needed
nodes.statement: Let $s_0 \rightarrow^* s_1 \rightarrow^* \cdots \rightarrow^* s_d \rightarrow^* \cdots \, s_\omega$ be a reduction to normal form of length at most $\omega$ such that, for all $d \in \mathbb{N}$, the steps in $s_d \twoheadrightarrow s_\omega$ occur below depth $d$ and $P_d$ is the set of positions in $s_d$ above depth $d$. If a redex in $s_0$ is essential for some $P_d$ in $s_0$ with $d \in \mathbb{N}$, then the redex is needed.
assumptions: $s_0 \rightarrow^* s_1 \rightarrow^* \cdots \rightarrow^* s_d \rightarrow^* \cdots \, s_\omega$ be a reduction to normal form of length at most $\omega$ such that, for all $d \in \mathbb{N}$, the steps in $s_d \twoheadrightarrow s_\omega$ occur below depth $d$ and $P_d$ is the set of positions in $s_d$ above depth $d$
a redex in $s_0$ is essential for some $P_d$ in $s_0$ with $d \in \mathbb{N}$
conclusions: the redex is needed

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.12
nodes.statement: \proof We reason by contradiction. Thus, suppose $u$ is a redex in $s_0$ that is essential for some prefix set $P_d$ but not needed. By definition of neededness there exists a reduction $s_0 = t_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_\alpha$ to normal form that does not contract any residual of $u$. Write $D_\alpha = (s_0 \rightarrow^* s_d) \mathord{\sslash} (t_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_\alpha)$, which exists by Lemma \ref{lem:nf_ok} and since $s_0 \rightarrow^* s_d$ can be seen as a finite sequence of complete developments, each consisting of a single step. We show by ordinal induction that a residual of $u$ occurs in $t_\alpha$, the first term of $D_\alpha$, that is essential for $P_d$. Obviously, for $t_0 = s_0$ the result is immediate by assumption. For $t_{\alpha + 1}$ the result follows by the induction hypothesis and Lemma \ref{lem:essstaysess}, since by assumption the redex contracted in $t_\alpha \rightarrow t_{\alpha + 1}$ is not a residual of $u$. For $t_\alpha$, with $\alpha$ a limit ordinal, the result follows by the induction hypothesis and strong convergence, since for some $\beta < \alpha$ we have by definition of the emaciated projection that $D_\alpha$ mirrors $(s_0 \rightarrow^* s_d) \mathord{\sslash} (t_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_\beta)$ in $P_d$. Hence, a residual of $u$ occurs in $t_\alpha$, contradicting that $t_\alpha$ is a normal form. Hence, every redex that is essential for some $P_d$ is needed. \qed
nodes.statement_short: By contradiction: along a normalising reduction avoiding $u$, ordinal induction with Lemma 4.24 keeps an essential residual of $u$ alive, contradicting normal form.

nodes.name: Assume not needed
nodes.statement: We reason by contradiction. Thus, suppose $u$ is a redex in $s_0$ that is essential for some prefix set $P_d$ but not needed. By definition of neededness there exists a reduction $s_0 = t_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_\alpha$ to normal form that does not contract any residual of $u$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $u$ essential but not needed; take a normalising reduction avoiding $u$.

nodes.name: Projection D_alpha
nodes.statement: Write $D_\alpha = (s_0 \rightarrow^* s_d) \mathord{\sslash} (t_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_\alpha)$, which exists by Lemma \ref{lem:nf_ok} and since $s_0 \rightarrow^* s_d$ can be seen as a finite sequence of complete developments, each consisting of a single step.
nodes.statement_short: Define $D_\alpha$, which exists by Lemma 4.28.

nodes.name: Essential residual persists
nodes.statement: We show by ordinal induction that a residual of $u$ occurs in $t_\alpha$, the first term of $D_\alpha$, that is essential for $P_d$. Obviously, for $t_0 = s_0$ the result is immediate by assumption. For $t_{\alpha + 1}$ the result follows by the induction hypothesis and Lemma \ref{lem:essstaysess}, since by assumption the redex contracted in $t_\alpha \rightarrow t_{\alpha + 1}$ is not a residual of $u$. For $t_\alpha$, with $\alpha$ a limit ordinal, the result follows by the induction hypothesis and strong convergence, since for some $\beta < \alpha$ we have by definition of the emaciated projection that $D_\alpha$ mirrors $(s_0 \rightarrow^* s_d) \mathord{\sslash} (t_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_\beta)$ in $P_d$.
nodes.statement_short: By ordinal induction an essential residual of $u$ survives.

nodes.name: Successor
nodes.statement: For $t_{\alpha + 1}$ the result follows by the induction hypothesis and Lemma \ref{lem:essstaysess}, since by assumption the redex contracted in $t_\alpha \rightarrow t_{\alpha + 1}$ is not a residual of $u$.
nodes.statement_short: Successor case by Lemma 4.24.

nodes.name: Limit
nodes.statement: For $t_\alpha$, with $\alpha$ a limit ordinal, the result follows by the induction hypothesis and strong convergence, since for some $\beta < \alpha$ we have by definition of the emaciated projection that $D_\alpha$ mirrors $(s_0 \rightarrow^* s_d) \mathord{\sslash} (t_0 \twoheadrightarrow t_\beta)$ in $P_d$.
nodes.statement_short: Limit case by strong convergence and mirroring.

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement: Hence, a residual of $u$ occurs in $t_\alpha$, contradicting that $t_\alpha$ is a normal form. Hence, every redex that is essential for some $P_d$ is needed.
nodes.statement_short: A residual in the normal form is a contradiction.

nodes.name: Needed redexes are essential
nodes.statement: Let $s_0 \rightarrow^* s_1 \rightarrow^* \cdots \rightarrow^* s_d \rightarrow^* \cdots \, s_\omega$ be a reduction to normal form of length at most $\omega$ such that, for all $d \in \mathbb{N}$, the steps in $s_d \twoheadrightarrow s_\omega$ occur below depth $d$ and $P_d$ is the set of positions in $s_d$ above depth $d$. If a redex in $s_0$ is needed, then there exists a $d \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the redex is essential for $P_d$ in $s_0$.
assumptions: $s_0 \rightarrow^* s_1 \rightarrow^* \cdots \rightarrow^* s_d \rightarrow^* \cdots \, s_\omega$ be a reduction to normal form of length at most $\omega$ such that, for all $d \in \mathbb{N}$, the steps in $s_d \twoheadrightarrow s_\omega$ occur below depth $d$ and $P_d$ is the set of positions in $s_d$ above depth $d$
a redex in $s_0$ is needed
conclusions: there exists a $d \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the redex is essential for $P_d$ in $s_0$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.13
nodes.statement: \proof Consider a reduction $S$ that contracts for increasingly larger $d \in \mathbb{N}$ all redexes essential for $P_d$, considering the emaciated projection of $s_0 \rightarrow^* s_d$, until such redexes no longer occur. It is possible to employ the emaciated projection by Lemma \ref{lem:nf_ok}. By Lemmas~\ref{lem:essential_then_decrease} and \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal} and the well-foundedness of $\prec$ it follows that $S$ is of length at most $\omega$. Moreover, again by Lemma \ref{lem:nf_ok} --- considering the emaciated projections of $s_0 \rightarrow^* s_e$ for all $e$ smaller than the $d$ under consideration at some point --- it follows that $S$ is strongly convergent. Hence, by Lemma \ref{lem:essstaysess} a redex can only be needed in $s_0$ if there exists some $d \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the redex is essential for $P_d$ in $s_0$. \qed
nodes.statement_short: Construct a strongly convergent normalising reduction contracting only essential redexes; by Lemma 4.24 inessential redexes are never contracted along it.

nodes.name: Construct S
nodes.statement: Consider a reduction $S$ that contracts for increasingly larger $d \in \mathbb{N}$ all redexes essential for $P_d$, considering the emaciated projection of $s_0 \rightarrow^* s_d$, until such redexes no longer occur. It is possible to employ the emaciated projection by Lemma \ref{lem:nf_ok}.
nodes.statement_short: Build $S$ contracting essential redexes for growing $d$.

nodes.name: Length at most omega
nodes.statement: By Lemmas~\ref{lem:essential_then_decrease} and \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal} and the well-foundedness of $\prec$ it follows that $S$ is of length at most $\omega$.
nodes.statement_short: Measure decrease bounds $S$ to length $\omega$.

nodes.name: Strong convergence
nodes.statement: Moreover, again by Lemma \ref{lem:nf_ok} --- considering the emaciated projections of $s_0 \rightarrow^* s_e$ for all $e$ smaller than the $d$ under consideration at some point --- it follows that $S$ is strongly convergent.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.28 gives strong convergence.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence, by Lemma \ref{lem:essstaysess} a redex can only be needed in $s_0$ if there exists some $d \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the redex is essential for $P_d$ in $s_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.24: only essential redexes can be needed.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.14
nodes.statement: Combining the above two lemmas, we obtain:
nodes.statement_short: Combine Lemmas 5.12 and 5.13.

nodes.name: Needed iff essential
nodes.statement: Let $s_0 \rightarrow^* s_1 \rightarrow^* \cdots \rightarrow^* s_d \rightarrow^* \cdots \, s_\omega$ be a reduction to normal form of length at most $\omega$ such that, for all $d \in \mathbb{N}$, the steps in $s_d \twoheadrightarrow t$ occur below depth $d$ and $P_d$ is the set of positions in $s_d$ above depth $d$. A redex in $s_0$ is needed if{f} there exists a $d \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the redex is essential for $P_d$ in $s_0$.

nodes.name: Needed-fair strategies are normalising
nodes.statement: If $s$ can be reduced to a normal form by a strongly convergent reduction, then it also reduces to a normal form by any needed-fair reduction. Any such reduction is strongly convergent and of length at most $\omega$.
assumptions: $s$ can be reduced to a normal form by a strongly convergent reduction
conclusions: it also reduces to a normal form by any needed-fair reduction
Any such reduction is strongly convergent and of length at most $\omega$.
nodes.label: thm:neededfair

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.15
nodes.statement: \proof By compression, we may assume we have a reduction $s \twoheadrightarrow t$ to normal form of length at most length $\omega$. Write the reduction as \[ s = s_0 \rightarrow^* s_1 \rightarrow^* \cdots \rightarrow^* s_d \rightarrow^* \cdots \, t \] with all steps in $s_d \twoheadrightarrow t$ occurring below depth $d$. Denote by $P_d$ the set of positions in $s_d$ above depth $d$. Consider the emaciated projection of a reduction $s \rightarrow^* s_d$ with respect to a prefix set $P_d$, which is possible by Lemma \ref{lem:nf_ok}. It follows by Lemma \ref{lem:essisneed} and the needed-fair condition that an essential redex is contracted after a finite number of steps as long as any essential redexes are left. As $\prec$ is well-founded, we now have by Lemmas \ref{lem:essential_then_decrease} and \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal} that the needed-fair reduction reduces $s$ to a term that mirrors $s_d$ in $P_d$ in a finite number of steps. Since the previous holds for any $s_d$ and $P_d$, it follows that any needed-fair reduction is a strongly convergent reduction to normal form of length at most $\omega$. \qed
nodes.statement_short: Compress to length $\omega$; for each depth, needed-fairness and Lemma 5.14 force essential redexes to be contracted, and the measure decrease reaches the normal form prefix in finitely many steps.

nodes.name: Compress and stratify
nodes.statement: By compression, we may assume we have a reduction $s \twoheadrightarrow t$ to normal form of length at most length $\omega$. Write the reduction as \[ s = s_0 \rightarrow^* s_1 \rightarrow^* \cdots \rightarrow^* s_d \rightarrow^* \cdots \, t \] with all steps in $s_d \twoheadrightarrow t$ occurring below depth $d$. Denote by $P_d$ the set of positions in $s_d$ above depth $d$.
nodes.statement_short: By compression take a normalising reduction of length at most $\omega$ stratified by depth.

nodes.name: Essential redexes get contracted
nodes.statement: Consider the emaciated projection of a reduction $s \rightarrow^* s_d$ with respect to a prefix set $P_d$, which is possible by Lemma \ref{lem:nf_ok}. It follows by Lemma \ref{lem:essisneed} and the needed-fair condition that an essential redex is contracted after a finite number of steps as long as any essential redexes are left.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.14 and needed-fairness: essential redexes are contracted.

nodes.name: Measure argument
nodes.statement: As $\prec$ is well-founded, we now have by Lemmas \ref{lem:essential_then_decrease} and \ref{lem:inessential_nonroot_then_equal} that the needed-fair reduction reduces $s$ to a term that mirrors $s_d$ in $P_d$ in a finite number of steps.
nodes.statement_short: Well-founded measure: mirroring $s_d$ on $P_d$ in finitely many steps.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Since the previous holds for any $s_d$ and $P_d$, it follows that any needed-fair reduction is a strongly convergent reduction to normal form of length at most $\omega$.
nodes.statement_short: Holding for all $d$ gives strong convergence to normal form.

nodes.name: First-order fair/outermost-fair/needed-fair reductions
nodes.statement: Consider the (first-order) iCRS consisting of the following three rules: \begin{align*} f(X,Y) & \rightarrow g(X, f(X, Y)) \\ a & \rightarrow b \\ c & \rightarrow c \end{align*} and consider the term $f(a,c)$. The reduction \[ f(a, c) \rightarrow g(a ,f(a,c)) \rightarrow g(b,f(a,c)) \rightarrow g(b,g(a,f(a,c))) \rightarrow \cdots \, , \] which alternates between contracting an $f(X, Y) \rightarrow g(X, f(X, Y))$-redex and an $a \rightarrow b$-redex, is easily shown to be outermost-fair and needed-fair contracting only outermost redexes. The reduction is not fair as no descendant of a $c \rightarrow c$-redex is ever reduced. Now consider the reduction \[ f(a, c) \rightarrow f(b, c) \rightarrow g(b ,f(b,c)) \rightarrow g(b,g(b,f(b,c))) \rightarrow g(b, g(b, g(b, f(b, c)))) \rightarrow \cdots \, , \] which first contracts the $a \rightarrow b$-redex and then keeps contracting $f(X, Y) \rightarrow g(X, f(X, Y))$-redexes; this reduction is easily shown to be outermost-fair and needed-fair, contracting only needed redexes. Note that the first redex contracted is not outermost and that the reduction is not fair as no descendant of a $c \rightarrow c$-redex is ever contracted. Finally, consider the reduction \[ f(a, c) \rightarrow f(b, c) \rightarrow f(b, c) \rightarrow g(b,f(b,c)) \rightarrow g(b,f(b,c)) \rightarrow g(b,g(b,f(b,c))) \rightarrow \cdots \, , \] which first contracts the $a \rightarrow b$-redex and then alternates between contracting a $c \rightarrow c$-redex and an $f(X, Y) \rightarrow g(X, f(X, Y))$-redex; this reduction is easily shown to be fair, outermost-fair, and needed-fair. All three reductions are strongly convergent, converging to the infinite term given by $s = g(b, s)$, which is clearly a normal form.
nodes.statement_short: Three reductions of $f(a,c)$ comparing outermost-fair, needed-fair and fair strategies, all converging to the normal form $s = g(b,s)$.

nodes.statement: Recall from \cite{KOR93,T03} that $\lambda$-calculus with $\beta$-reduction can be fully and faithfully modelled as a CRS; likewise, i$\lambda$c\xspace with $\beta$-reduction can be modelled fully and faithfully by an iCRS \cite{JJ05a,paper_i}.

nodes.statement: The standard way of doing so is by introducing explicit symbols $\mathtt{app}$ and $\mathtt{abs}$ for application and abstraction, respectively, and defining the $\beta$-rule as \[ \mathtt{app}(\mathtt{abs}([x]Z(x)),Z') \rightarrow Z(Z') \]

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 2.31
nodes.statement: \proof As each path projection derives from a path, we have by definition that $\phi$ is \emph{surjective}. Similar for the path projections in $\mathcal{P}(s, \mathcal{U})$ and the maximal paths, as each path projection in $\mathcal{P}(s, \mathcal{U})$ derives from a maximal path. To prove that $\phi$ is \emph{injective}, suppose there exist (maximal) paths $\Pi, \Pi'$ such that $\phi(\Pi) = \phi(\Pi')$. By definition of $\phi$ both paths and the path projection consist of the same number of nodes and edges. Let $\Pi^*$ be the longest shared prefix of $\Pi$ and $\Pi'$. The prefix $\Pi^*$ is non-empty, as any path of $s$ starts with $(s, \epsilon)$. There are now two cases to consider depending on $\Pi^*$ ending in either an edge or a node. In case $\Pi^*$ ends in an edge, the next node is uniquely determined by the definition of paths. Hence, as $\Pi$ and $\Pi'$ have the same number of nodes and edges we can extend $\Pi^*$ with that unique node, contradiction. In case $\Pi^*$ ends in a node, both paths extend $\Pi^*$, otherwise $\Pi = \Pi'$ or the paths differ in the number of nodes or edges. In case the extension is with an unlabelled edge in case of one of the paths, the other path must also extend $\Pi^*$ with an unlabelled edge. This follows by the definition of paths. In case the extension is with an edge labelled $i$, the other path must also extend $\Pi^*$ with an edge labelled $i$. This follows by definition of paths and by $\phi(\Pi) = \phi(\Pi')$. Hence, in case $\Pi^*$ ends in a node a contradiction also follows. We can conclude that $\phi$ is an injection both between paths and path projections and between maximal paths and the path projections in $\mathcal{P}(s, \mathcal{U})$. \qed
nodes.statement_short: Surjectivity by definition; injectivity by contradiction on the longest shared prefix of two paths with equal projection, splitting on whether it ends in an edge or a node.
